solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hauled into court, after work, I get in bother

indicators.note: being hauled into something means being dragged inside it, so the next pieces go inside
the I comes after the piece for work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone dragged before the judges straight after a shift finds themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' and 'work' are read as everyday crossword abbreviations, not as a trial and a job; the answer is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase means to be in trouble or to be punished, so getting in bother fits.

clue.text: Tweets I'd picked up in street near St Paul's

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the clue's words are taken by their sound

parts.note: tweets are cheeps, the chirps of birds, followed by I'd

explanation.surface: Someone overheard birdsong in a London street close to the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAPSIDE is a historic street in the City of London, beside St Paul's Cathedral; 'cheeps I'd' sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: This old market thoroughfare runs right past the cathedral in London's financial district.

clue.text: Former racing champ's endless resentment

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Nelson Piquet was a Formula One world champion in the 1980s

explanation.surface: A retired motor-racing champion nurses a grudge that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last T from PIQUET, the Brazilian driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or wounded pride, a close synonym of resentment.

clue.text: After end of shift, more than one scaffolder sets off

indicators.note: the scaffolders' word comes after the letter taken from shift
the end of the word shift is its final letter

parts.note: riggers are workers who put up scaffolding, and the plural covers more than one

explanation.surface: When the shift finishes, several scaffolders head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes T from shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something off is to start it, which is what a trigger does, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: That poses problem immediately

indicators.note: a problem is something tangled, so these letters must be sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Whatever poses a difficulty should be dealt with at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges THAT POSES.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means with great speed, the way an urgent letter was once sent by express post.

clue.text: Old man in great discomfort

parts.note: an old man is informal for father, which is pa

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman is suffering badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe discomfort is a straightforward synonym for suffering of this kind.

clue.text: Restaurant's signature dish is plaice cooked with tasty coating

indicators.note: cooked fish is changed from its raw state, so the letters are reworked
the coating of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The house dish is plaice prepared in a delicious crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges IS PLAICE into SPECIALI; 'coating' adds TY, the outsides of tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish a restaurant is known for is called its speciality, the item it does best.

clue.text: Respect a great leader in the House?

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for house

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An MP shows esteem for a towering party leader in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes G from great; with A it goes inside HOME. 'the House' looks like Parliament but is just a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or tribute, a formal kind of respect.

clue.text: Choose record recently released?

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
a new record that is out has just been released

explanation.surface: Someone is picking out a disc that has just come on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To select one from a group is to pick it, as when choosing a person for praise.

clue.text: Last of the useless glue

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: poxy is British slang for worthless or rubbish

explanation.surface: The final tube of adhesive is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' takes E from the; POXY is informal British for shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy resin is a strong two-part adhesive, so it is a kind of glue.

clue.text: Old pretty clothing is dellicate

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: clothing wraps around, so the word pretty encloses is

parts.note: pretty can mean fairly, which is quite

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned, pretty outfit is fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like an adjective for the clothes but means fairly; the blog's text spells delicate with a double L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exquisite is finely made and refined, the sense of delicate craftsmanship.

clue.text: Fruit brought in from Angola

indicators.note: the letters are carried inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Produce has been imported from an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' finds the letters across from Angola.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Promise given by Heath briefly chasing power

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the actor's trimmed name follows the P

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Heath Ledger was an Australian actor

explanation.surface: A vow is made by Heath, quickly going after power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests former Prime Minister Edward Heath, but it is Heath Ledger; 'briefly' trims him to LEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn undertaking, a synonym of promise as a noun.

clue.text: One of two books left by the old retired writer

parts.note: the Old Testament has two books of Kings, so either is Kings

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the old word for the is turned round

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A retired author leaves behind one of a pair of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Kingsley wrote The Water-Babies; Kingsley Amis is another candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley was a Victorian novelist, so the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Hostile towards northern town

parts.note: warring sides are hostile to each other
to means towards

explanation.surface: Someone is unfriendly to a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: WARRINGTON is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large Cheshire settlement between Liverpool and Manchester, so it is a town.

clue.text: Supply dope to friend in relaxed fashion

indicators.note: to joins the friend on after the first piece

parts.note: dope is slang for information, so supplying it is to inform
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone passes drugs to a pal in a laid-back way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something casually, without ceremony, is the same as doing it in a relaxed manner.

clue.text: Warning device installed by the company is the genuine article

indicators.note: something installed by the firm sits inside it

parts.note: a firm is a company
real means genuine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A safety alarm fitted by the firm is the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the genuine article' reads as a set phrase but splits into genuine and article.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sounds when smoke or flames are detected is a warning device.

clue.text: Work steadily, having entered old college

indicators.note: the small piece goes inside the verb

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade steadily

explanation.surface: Someone studies hard after enrolling at a former college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having entered' puts O inside PLY. A poly, short for polytechnic, was a British higher-education college; most became universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A poly was a British polytechnic, a kind of college for higher education.

clue.text: Singers, those making loud noise about excessive drug-taking?

indicators.note: about means around, so the noisy people enclose the overdose

parts.note: yellers are people who shout
OD stands for overdose

explanation.surface: Loud singers are blamed for taking too many drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Yodellers are Alpine singers who flip between chest voice and falsetto.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine performers who warble between chest and falsetto voice are a kind of singer.

clue.text: Protective garment over one single item of underwear

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, protecting against rain
I is the Roman numeral one
sole means single, the only one

explanation.surface: A protective coat is worn over a single piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as layering clothes, but in a down clue it turns the raincoat word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a loose sleeveless top worn as lingerie, so it is an item of underwear.

clue.text: There's merit in learning

indicators.note: in shows that the letters lie inside the next word

explanation.surface: Studying is a worthwhile pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds the letters within learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, and to deserve is to earn, as a verb.

clue.text: Lengthy pamphlet checked by professional editor

indicators.note: checked by means held in by the two people that follow

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A long leaflet is proofread by an expert editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checked by' suggests proofreading, but it means held in by the two people that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn out in time is prolonged, so it means lengthy.

clue.text: Outlaw secures shelter in Asian kingdom

indicators.note: secures means holds tight, so the ban encloses the shelter

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A fugitive finds refuge in an Asian monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a fugitive but is the verb ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhutan is a Himalayan country ruled by a king, so it is an Asian kingdom.

clue.text: Wicked acts of vandalism

definitions.meaning: wicked is slang for excellent or great
breaking windows and property is destructive damage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like evil, but both words are slang for terrific.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is British slang for excellent, and also the act of breaking things up.

clue.text: Various European kids took part in winter sport

indicators.note: various means assorted, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Children from across Europe went to the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges E and KIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gone down the slopes on skis is to have taken part in a winter sport.

clue.text: Driver shells out at regular intervals for fuel

indicators.note: out at regular intervals means alternate letters are taken from the two words

explanation.surface: A motorist pays up for petrol every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shells out' looks like paying, but 'out at regular intervals' takes D, I, E, S, E, L from Driver shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy oil used to power engines, so it is a fuel.

clue.text: River trip begins with introduction from steward

indicators.note: begins with puts the steward's letter at the front of the trip
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: A boat trip starts with a welcome from the steward.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, in Kent, Dorset and Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is a river in southern and eastern England.

clue.text: Fashion world of Jean-Paul Gaultier is heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing its middle letter

parts.note: the French designer would call the world le monde

explanation.surface: The French designer's fashion scene is cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is heartless' drops the middle N of MONDE, French for world.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style or fashion, the sense in a la mode.

clue.text: Doze off during sex? That's —

indicators.note: during means inside the period of, so the doze sits within

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex
a nap is a short doze

explanation.surface: Falling asleep in bed with a partner would be unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash is a blank for the answer to fill, completing the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing at such a moment would be unsuitable, which is what the word means when it fills the blank.

clue.text: New roof to order? here's money-saving offer

indicators.note: putting letters to order arranges them anew

explanation.surface: A shop promotes new roofs made to order as a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges NEW ROOF TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A buy-one-get-one-free deal halves the price per item, a classic money-saving promotion.

clue.text: Right ignored in reshuffle by D Cameron in power

indicators.note: a reshuffle mixes things up, as in a cabinet reshuffle, so the letters are rearranged
ignored means a letter is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle by the Prime Minister passed over the right wing while he held power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' takes R out of D CAMERON IN, and 'reshuffle' rearranges what is left, DCAMEONIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is control or supremacy, which is power over others.

clue.text: Certain winds about middle of January — such as this one?

definitions.text: Certain winds about middle of January — such as this one?

indicators.note: winds means wraps around, so the turned word goes round the central letter
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Some winds blow around mid-January, perhaps like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SURE to ERUS, and 'winds' wraps it round U, the middle of January. Eurus was the Greek god of the east wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurus was the ancient Greek god of the east wind, so this is a wind of that kind.
